title: Field-tuned incommensurate fan phase in an Ising-like triangular antiferromagnet
authors: D. Flavián, R. Okuma, P. Manuel, Q. Huang, H. Zhou, R. Coldea
abstract: Using single-crystal neutron diffraction we report the observation of a field-tuned incommensurate phase in a field range just below magnetization saturation in the Ising-like triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$. This phase occurs for magnetic fields applied along the Ising axis and exhibits an in-plane incommensurate propagation vector that moves along the hexagonal Brillouin zone boundary upon varying field, challenging the simple $XXZ$ antiferromagnetic description of the system. Within a semiclassical framework, we successfully identify this pre-saturation phase as a coplanar fan phase and study the role of dipole-dipole interactions and bond-dependent exchange anisotropy in its stabilization mechanism. We additionally present a minimal exchange model including interlayer couplings, which reproduces the complex magnetic phase diagram in field including the observed field-dependence of the incommensurate propagation vector in the fan phase.
summary: This work reports experimental evidence for a field-tuned incommensurate fan phase in $	ext{Na}_2	ext{BaCo}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$ using neutron diffraction. By combining this data with theoretical modeling, the authors argue that dipole-dipole interactions are crucial for stabilizing this complex magnetic state. The paper successfully refines the underlying spin Hamiltonian to account for the observed field dependence of the incommensurate propagation vector.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the nature of a field-tuned incommensurate fan phase observed in an Ising-like triangular antiferromagnet, which challenges simple theoretical descriptions.
main_result: The authors identify this pre-saturation phase as a coplanar fan phase stabilized by dipole-dipole interactions and bond-dependent exchange anisotropy. They propose a refined spin Hamiltonian that successfully reproduces the complex magnetic phase diagram observed experimentally.
method: The research combines single-crystal neutron diffraction experiments with theoretical modeling using semiclassical Linear Spin Wave Theory (LSWT) and mean-field analysis.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Na}_2	ext{BaCo}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$, an Ising-like triangular-lattice antiferromagnet. The physics is modeled by anisotropic Hamiltonians, requiring the inclusion of dipole-dipole couplings and bond-dependent exchange terms beyond simple nearest-neighbor XXZ models.
key_observables: Magnetic Bragg peaks with field-dependent incommensurate propagation vectors ($\mathbf{Q}$), particularly showing movement along the hexagonal Brillouin zone boundary from K towards M points.
important_parameters: Applied magnetic field ($H$), temperature (down to 0.05 K), and coupling constants related to exchange anisotropy ($\Delta$) and dipolar interactions.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on semiclassical approximations, treating dipole-dipole coupling as a small source of bond-dependent anisotropy, and using nearest-neighbor approximations for long-range interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, representative neutron diffraction maps showing varying $q_z$ components across different magnetic phases (I-III), and critically, the continuous movement of a magnetic Bragg peak in Phase IV as a function of applied field H.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from presenting experimental observations of novel incommensurate peaks to developing theoretical frameworks. It first establishes the limitations of simple XXZ models, then incorporates dipolar couplings via LSWT to explain the observed field-dependent fan phase, culminating in a minimal exchange model that reproduces the full magnetic phase diagram.
why_interesting: The detailed study of how long-range interactions (dipolar coupling) stabilize exotic phases like the fan phase provides insights into emergent quantum magnetism and frustrated lattice models relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.
